pr_body:
Solves https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104731

This PR adds mappings for OpenTelemetry data via a new plugin `otel-data`

The PR is mainly based on:
- the existing apm-data plugin from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/97546
- the https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104455 draft PR by @felixbarny - most of the mappings are from there

What happens in the PR:
- Created `YamlTemplateRegistry` as an abstract base class that loads mappings from YAML. The code of this class comes from `APMIndexTemplateRegistry` which now derives from `YamlTemplateRegistry`. The shared code is now moved to `core`.
- Added `otel-data` plugin with `OtelIndexTemplateRegistry` which also derives from `YamlTemplateRegistry`.
- Moved the mappings into YAML files from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104455.

TODOs:
- [x] Discuss if we want to share some mappings between APM and OTel (candidates: all traces@ files from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104455), those are currently not yet in the PR -> ~Discussed: not at this point~ Update: we did that - now some some basic things are shared across otel and apm.
- [x] Discuss data stream lifecycle for OTel mappings (right now, nothing is set in the PR) -> Discussed: Since these mappings are shared across multiple OTel use-cases (e.g. system metrics and APM, for now we don't set a default ILM/DSL, since it's hard to come up with a default. Using what APM does today may not be good for integrations - so for now no DSL is set in these templates).
- [x] Adding more tests to `otel-data`

Hi @GregKalapos, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

> Hi @gregkalapos, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

Why?! I tried to be a proper contributor and added the related issue - now the bot removes it. :(

> why are these being managed in yaml instead of matching the existing precedent of having them in json? I find yaml much more error-prone for unintentional changes, since it is heavily indentation reliant.

@dakrone that's my doing. We have historically had far more issues with business logic (wrong mappings, dynamic templates, etc.) than with syntax (indentation, "Norway problem", etc.). So we're optimising for readability and the ability to comment. Comprehensive (YAML) REST tests will cover basic syntax issues.

> > why are these being managed in yaml instead of matching the existing precedent of having them in json? I find yaml much more error-prone for unintentional changes, since it is heavily indentation reliant.

So we're optimising for readability and the ability to comment. Comprehensive (YAML) REST tests will cover basic syntax issues.

Yeah, so I took yaml, because `apm-data` already used yaml and we also discussed with @felixbarny and we said we'd move the json from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104455 to yaml. I'm personally fine with both, but my 2 cents is that apm and otel should use the same, because it'll be maintained by the same team. So with that I'd have a slight preference to move on with yaml for consistency.

There are already tests here that load these mappings and checks for them, so I'm less worried about accidental wrong indentation.
@gregkalapos I see you removed summary_gauge & summary_counter, but summary_metrics doesn't have time_series_metric. Should we add that? I think with "counter"?

> @gregkalapos I see you removed summary_gauge & summary_counter, but summary_metrics doesn't have time_series_metric. Should we add that? I think with "counter"?

I'm not sure if it makes much of a difference. I suppose it's relevant for downsampling. I'm not sure if counter or gauge is most appropriate here. The reason we removed summary_gauge & summary_counter is that there's no temporality for summary metrics. It's also not always monotonically increasing as it depends on the start and end timestamp. So you can effectively have either temporality without really having an indication of what the temporality is. At least that's my understanding of it @lahsivjar, please correct me if I'm wrong.

For now, I'm in inclined to just leave out time_series_metric and then potentially add one in a follow-up.

I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/111877 to collect follow up issues. Feel free to add to it if I missed something.

The new `otel-data` plugin is disabled by default. Since there are multiple things going in this PR - as discussed in other meetings - we should cut here and merge if this is ok to go. With that, other teams can test this more easily. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/111877 will address remaining non-blockers.

review_comment: Presumably we will go through a similar process as we did for apm-data, staged rollout in serverless, let it soak, then enable by default everywhere? Would it be worth adding a NOTE comment here, so it's clear to readers why it's disabled by default now, and when they can expect that to change?

The reason for `false` was more that this is super early stage and we wanted to make it opt-in at this point. But adding a comment makes sense - I added one explaining the reasons.

>  staged rollout in serverless, let it soak, then enable by default everywhere

Wasn't aware of this, very useful! Also mentioned this in the comment - I feel we should sync on this and the strategy on when we move to `true` here later.
Thanks for the comment. SGTM, let's chat about it later

I'm wondering whether we should call the plugin just `otel`. That may be more future-proof in case we want to also add something like an OTLP endpoint to ES at some point. Having said that, `otel-data` may still be fitting and if not we could also just rename the module.

FWIW the "apm-data" plugin was originally just called "x-pack-apm", and was renamed because it introduced confusion with modules/apm. I could see the same thing happening with otel, though maybe if you get in first it doesn't matter ;)
